title: Aria
identity: The saxophone catalog entry is a Marty Lenard arrangement of Fabian Rehfeld’s *Aria*, Dorn Publications DORN2013, offered for B-flat or E-flat saxophone and piano. IMSLP’s record and public scan identify the original Rehfeld Op. 67 as a late-19th-century violin or cello work with piano or organ, so the saxophone item is a transcription of another instrumental piece.

evidence.claim: Current catalog lead identifies DORN2013 and the B-flat/E-flat saxophone and piano edition arranged by Marty Lenard.
IMSLP identifies Op. 67, first published in 1895, as for violin or cello with piano or organ; the public scan is a violin score.
The public scan shows an Adagio molto sostenuto opening in the violin part. This observation is about the source violin score only, not the saxophone arrangement.
evidence.source_name: Public-domain Rehfeld source score, digitized from the 1918 Oliver Ditson edition

score_observations.claim: Printed p. 32 opens Adagio molto sostenuto, with long tied notes in the violin/cello line over sustained piano chords that become more mobile with chromatic inflections; later on the same page the solo line briefly breaks into quicker notes before returning to a quiet dolcissimo statement. This is the original violin/cello score, not the saxophone arrangement.

review_focus: Inference: compare the saxophone arrangement with the source’s slow sustained violin writing; inspect the sax edition directly before assessing range or articulation.
collection_flag: Documented transcription of Rehfeld’s original violin/cello work; separate saxophone arrangement lists two saxophone transpositions. Original intended audience is not established by the sources found.

score_links.description: Original violin/cello and piano/organ score, not the saxophone arrangement.

gaps: The Dorn saxophone arrangement was not inspected, so its relation to the source, transposition, and saxophone-specific demands remain unknown.
